Wedding Transportation in Scottsdale

Scottsdale Sprinters runs wedding guest shuttles from $185 an hour on the Mini Bus (24 Pax), Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and 56-Passenger Motorcoach, and carries the couple in the Executive White Sprinter or Executive Black Sprinter, or the whole wedding party in the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax). 8 chauffeured vehicles are on the wedding list, seating 14 to 56, from $145 an hour on a 4-hour minimum — so a 12-hour wedding day, which earns 2 free hours, bills 10. Call (623) 986-6339.

Last updated: September 24, 2026

What does wedding transportation in Scottsdale cover?

Two jobs on one reservation: a guest shuttle between hotel and venue, and a car for the couple and the wedding party. 8 vehicles are on the wedding list, seating 14 to 56, from $145 an hour on a 4-hour minimum. Everything is chauffeured and booked by the hour, so the vehicle stays for the whole block rather than leaving between movements. Stops cost nothing on an hourly charter, so the getting-ready pickup, the ceremony run and the late return belong on one booking. The office states the service limit in its own words: "Hourly charters start at four hours on every vehicle except the 56-passenger motorcoach, which starts at five. The motorcoach is the largest single vehicle we run; a full guest shuttle beyond that is a coordinated multi-vehicle fleet on one reservation. Anything the online quote cannot price — an unusual route, a multi-vehicle movement, a vehicle we hold for request only — goes to the reservations desk and comes back as a written quote before any card is charged."

What is a wedding bus, and which one do we run?

A wedding bus is a chauffeured bus booked by the hour for one wedding day. 4 vehicles above do that job, seating 24 to 56 from $185 an hour; the wedding party bus is a different cabin, the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) at $175 an hour, on a 4-hour minimum. Shuttle buses for weddings are the 4 units at or above the 20-passenger line — Mini Bus (24 Pax) through 56-Passenger Motorcoach — and their job is the guest list. Bridal party transportation is the work below it, where the cabin matters more than the seat count. The two are not one booking. A wedding party bus is a lounge cabin for the people standing up with the couple — Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) or Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter. Guest wedding buses divide down per seat instead: $31 on the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax), $29 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Both can ride one reservation.

How does a hotel-to-venue guest shuttle actually run?

As timed waves rather than a timetable. One Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) carries 29 guests a run, so two runs move 58; the 56-Passenger Motorcoach takes 56 in a single load. The hours are already bought, so an extra wave costs nothing. A guest shuttle is three movements dressed as one: hotel to venue before the ceremony, venue to reception when those differ, and reception back to the hotel at the end. Waves beat one oversized load: an early run, a main run, a last run for whoever stays. Nothing here is a published interval, and we will not print one: a circuit depends on the two addresses and on what the venue does with a commercial vehicle. Give us the movements and the times you need, and the loop comes back agreed in writing, vehicle named.

Which vehicle seats your guest list?

Up to 24 guests fit the Mini Bus (24 Pax); up to 27 the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax); up to 29 the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax); up to 56 the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Past 56 in one load it becomes several vehicles on one reservation. Read the seat count as a hard limit, not a target. A wedding rides with dresses, suit bags, gifts and florals, and those occupy the same vehicle the guests do. Units the owner runs more than one of can run in parallel, up to 3 of one unit (Up to 87 across 3 Executive Mini Coaches); past that the charter bus rental guide covers the coach class and the desk quotes the movement in writing. What do the couple and the wedding party ride in?

4 vehicles below the 20-passenger line do that work, seating 14 to 16 from $145 an hour. The Executive White Sprinter is the couple's own car; the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) is the lounge the wedding party travels in together. The difference is the cabin, not the badge. An executive Sprinter is forward-facing seats with a separate rear compartment — what a dress, a veil and a photographer's bag need. A lounge cabin is inward-facing benches, which is what the wedding party wants between ceremony and reception. Bags decide more wedding bookings than seats. The office puts it plainly: "Dresses, suit bags, florals and gifts all need somewhere to sit. Tell us what is traveling with the party when you request the quote so the fit is confirmed in writing." The 56-Passenger Motorcoach publishes room for 125 bags; the Mini Bus (24 Pax) publishes no number, so its fit is confirmed in writing.

What does a wedding day cost, and what is included?

A published 12-hour wedding day earns 2 free hours, so it bills 10: $1,450 in the Executive White Sprinter, $2,250 in the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax), before 8% Arizona tax. A shorter booking still bills the 4-hour minimum, and the clock runs from the first pickup to the last drop-off. Included: the vehicle, the chauffeur and the fuel. Not included: checkout add-ons, hours past the window, and what a property charges a commercial vehicle for access. Extra stops are free on an hourly charter; on a transfer each is $50. Per guest, the pricing page's own method splits the fare across every seat: the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) minimum, $900 across 29, is $31 a seat; the 56-Passenger Motorcoach minimum, $1,625 across 56, is $29. A second wave inside the same block adds riders, not hours. Two house rules matter here: "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." and "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really." Service areas: Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley; the charge is time rather than distance. The figures above are the current published hourly rates — what the checkout charges today, not a quoted total for your day. Request a current quote with your date, addresses and headcount.

How do you lay out the day's timeline and addresses?

As 4 separate movements with real addresses, not one round trip with implied stops. Name one point person we call — not the couple — and put any venue entrance instruction on the booking. Every stop on a 4-hour hourly charter is free. This is the sequence the office asks for, in its own words: "Write every address on the reservation as its own movement — getting-ready location, ceremony, reception, hotel — rather than describing the day as a round trip with implied stops. Name one point person we call on the day; it should not be the couple. Where a venue directs commercial vehicles to a particular entrance, put that instruction on the booking and the chauffeur will work from it." Work the timeline backwards from the ceremony and end the block a little after the last movement; between distant movements the vehicle simply waits. Getting-ready location Ceremony Reception Hotel

How do out-of-town guests get in from Phoenix Sky Harbor?

As transfers rather than hourly time when they land together: $295 one way in the Executive Black Sprinter, $550 in the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax), with $50 per extra stop and no hourly minimum at all on a transfer. Arrivals spread across a day are a wave instead. A transfer is priced as a trip rather than by the clock, which is why it suits one flight carrying a block of guests to one hotel. Inside an hourly block the vehicle is already bought, so repeating the airport run costs nothing. One wedding can carry both: a transfer for the arrivals day, an hourly block for the wedding day.

How do the deposit and the wedding cancellation window work?

A 50% deposit holds the vehicle and the balance is charged 48 hours before pickup, plus 8% Arizona tax. Weddings sit in the large-group tier, so the window is 30 days rather than the standard one, with keep-the-deposit terms down to 14 days and nothing refunded inside that. The tier is not a judgement call. 20 or more passengers, or 2 or more vehicles, is a large group in the refund code, and the published policy says so directly: "Large groups, party buses and weddings (20+ passengers or two or more vehicles) get a full refund 30 or more days out and keep-the-deposit terms down to 14 days." The wedding page states the same thing in its own operational block: "Weddings, party buses and any booking of 20+ passengers or two or more vehicles carry the large-group cancellation window rather than the standard one." Anything the online quote cannot price goes to the desk. Call (623) 986-6339 with the movements, the headcount and the addresses, and it comes back in writing with each vehicle named.
